messages.subject: Software warning - Error
messages.body_plain:
Dear list,

I frequently get from my projects a warning message when I try to open =
them. The bad thing is, once this warning comes up, I usually have to do =

it all again, once I can not recover my project.

My operating system is Mac, although I run Distance software using =
Virtual Box, which is a cross-platform virtualization application, as a =

lot of you might konw.

This is the message I get:

The following internal error has occurred in Distance

Unexpected error in Distance Database Engine.
Source: D6DbEng.ProjectDatabase.OpenJetDatabase
internal Error number: 3197

Internal Error description: "The Microsoft Jet database engine stopped =
the process because you and a another user are attempting to change the =

same data at the same time."

(Error raised from: Distance.ClsProject.OpenProjectDatabase)
(Error source: D6DbEng.ProjectDatabase.OpenJetDatabase)
(Error number: -2147211505)

If you suspect this error is caused by a bug in the program, please note =

down all the above information and contact the program authors.

Press Ok and Distance will try to recover from the error.
Press Help for more information about internal erros in Distance.

Is there anything to do?

Thank you,=20

Carlos Benfica.

-------------------------------------
   Carlos Eduardo Benfica
31 - 2514.3303 / 9677.0003
-------------------------------------

--

messages.subject: compare results with different series expansions
messages.subject_clean: compare results with different series expansions
messages.body_plain:
Dear Forum,

I'm busy using Distance to obtain densities of a primate species in 4
forests. Once obtained the estimates I wanted to compare them statistically.
I have a very immediate question: can I compare results obtained with
different series expansions of the same key function?

this is an example of my function selection using AIC:

*DATASET*

*FOREST*

*KEY FUNCTION*

*SERIES EXPANSION*

*Species*

Magombera

Half-normal

Hermite polynomial

* *

Matundu

Half-normal

Cosine

* *

Mwanihana

Half-normal

Hermite polynomial

* *

Uzungwa Scarp Forest Reserve

Half-normal

Cosine

Can I compare the results?

Thank you very much for your help

Best regards
Alessandro Araldi
--

Alessandro Araldi
Wildlife Biologist
via Metastasio 23/13
10132 Torino, Italy
Tel.: +393490687718

messages.body_plain:
Alessandro:

Yes you can compare density estimates of data fitted with different
series expansion models.  The nature of the data determine the detection
function appropriate for them.  Have a look at Section 3.6.4 of Buckland
et al. (2001) on the subject of estimating change in density for the
case of comparing between pairs of estimates.

messages.subject: Estimating g(0) for passive acoustic surveys
messages.subject_clean: Estimating g(0) for passive acoustic surveys
messages.body_plain:
Dear List

I am conducting Distance analysis on data collected during a passive
acoustic survey for harbour porpoises in the North Sea in November.  We had
13 sightings during the survey and over 200 usable detections.  I am now
looking into how to calculate the g(0) for this survey.

One way of calculating the g(0) which has been suggested to me by more
experienced scientists in Distance sampling is to compare the number of
sightings with the number of sightings which have detections (13 sightings,
7 of which have corresponding acoustic detections).  This method provides me
with an estimate of g(0) around 0.46 which I believe is extremely low.

To me, this seems to ignore the fact that although only 7 of the 13
sightings had corresponding detections, we had 235 detections during this
time.  Additionally being a winter survey in the North Sea, the sighting
conditions were very poor and very few of the sightings occurred in sea
states less than 3.  Is there a way of including all the encounters (235+13)
and calculating the g(0)  by the number of encounters that were missed (this
gives me a much higher g(0) value of around 0.9). To me this seems much more
accurate, as I would be worried that by using the other technique the end
abundance estimates would be overestimated, however as these are widely
different.

Any suggestions or guidance on this topic would be much appreciated.

Many thanks in advance,

Anna

Anna Cucknell

Marine Conservation Research Ltd.

Marine Conservation Research International

messages.subject: Re: Estimating g(0) for passive acoustic surveys
messages.subject_clean: Estimating g(0) for passive acoustic surveys
messages.body_plain:
It could be too low if there is negative dependence between visual and
acoustic detections which is very likely.  Negative dependence means what
can be heard can't be seen and what can be seen can't be heard to some
degree.  Typically with methods using dual visual observers the dependence
is positive which can mean g(0) estimate is too high. But with different
detection techniques the dependence can be negative.  I believe this is
written up in a report on acoustic methods for marine mammal surveys that I
attended a number of years ago in San Diego.

regards --jeff
